where.screen_path: library + feature internals (no UI this turn)

summary: Phase 5c-i-β — the Nostr wire client. Substrate-agnostic Transport interface; minimal Nostr WebSocket client with auto-reconnect and id-dedup; encrypted-inbox layer that wraps each tapit-attest envelope in NIP-44 ciphertext addressed to one recipient and unwraps incoming events back to typed Attestation objects (dropping tampered, wrong-recipient, and junk events silently). Default replaceable relay set ships with the wallet (D-11a). tapit-attest got a small signDigest export so the wallet does not re-implement Schnorr for Nostr event ids. 10 new tests; all eight gates green; pushed branch-only.

why.text: Phase 5c needs the wallet to send and receive encrypted envelopes across Nostr relays. NIP-44 (5c-i-α) gave us the payload format; this cut gives us the wire. The interface is substrate-agnostic because D-06 says the substrate is swappable and never a hard dependency — Nostr is the default, not the only path. Tapit envelopes ride inside a custom event kind (9573, regular events that relays persist for async delivery) per D-11c. The wallet key doubles as the Nostr identity per D-11d.

outcome.notes: Pushed to claude/compare-library-wallet-OW5FF as commit 5f65f3c. NOT pushed to main — operator has not said the word for this cut. Transport feature tree-shakes out of the bundle for now (no runtime importer); will appear once 5c-i-γ wires it to connections. Noted a pre-existing flake in tapit-attest's encryption tampered-byte test (1/256 chance the random ciphertext byte at position 0 is 0x00 and the corruption is a no-op) — unrelated to this cut, passed on retry, surfaced in opinions.

uncertainty: The NostrTransport is wire-protocol-correct per NIP-01 and verified via injected fake WebSocket, but it has not been pointed at a real public relay yet. Once 5c-i-γ wires the inbox up and the operator does a smoke test with two devices, the round-trip-against-real-relays evidence will arrive. The Nostr event kind 9573 was picked because it is in the regular-event range and not assigned to any major NIP — if a future NIP claims it, we swap the constant.
ripple: app-connections — will become the consumer of sendEnvelopeTo/subscribeInbox in 5c-i-γ (an in-person handshake gains an async path)
next: Cut Phase 5c-i-γ — wire the transport into the connections feature so an existing in-person flow (handshake or membership) can also travel async through Nostr. Likely: a hook that opens a NostrTransport for the wallet, a subscribeInbox subscription that routes incoming envelopes to the right cosign/absorb modal, and a 'send remotely' option on the handshake modal.
